note.after_visit_summary: Your mood has been stable, and your bipolar II disorder is well-controlled on lamotrigine 200 mg daily. You sleep about 7 hours regularly and take your medication most days, though you sometimes forget a dose. You have no rash or mouth sores. You are planning to start combination birth control pills next month, which can lower lamotrigine levels in your blood. To make sure your medication still works, we will check your lamotrigine blood level this week before you start the pill, and again 2 to 3 weeks after you begin it. If needed, we will adjust your dose. If you prefer, progestin-only pills or an IUD are options that won’t affect your lamotrigine—discuss these with your gynecologist. Continue your multivitamin. If you develop a rash with fever or mouth sores, stop lamotrigine and seek emergency care. If you miss 5 or more doses in a row, do not restart at 200 mg without calling us first. We will call your lab results to 317-555-0172. Return in 3 months, or sooner if your medication or birth control plan changes.
